EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  JUNE 24, 2019

A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order by CHAIR HUFF at 7:00 p.m.

Committee Members Present:  Huff, Brtis, Ciarolla, Martin, Silvano, Shinn, Zigrang

Committee Members Absent:  Dean-Porter, Harik

City Staff Present: Assistant to the City Manager, Alexa Davis
  Community Services Coordinator Daniel A-Haja
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith

DRAFT MINUTES OF JANUARY 28, 2019
MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE APRIL 29, 2019 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN HUFF SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
Bob and Joann Bennett, Pony Lane, expressed concern about fences being down and the
storm drain at catch basin not properly accepting water possibly as a result of the CalWater
project. California Water Service (CalWater) Representative, Karina Winje, indicated that the
area along Palomino Trail does not have the storm drain completed yet. Residents and
CalWater will meet together at site to discuss concerns further.

MEMBER BRTIS asked who is responsible of restoration of trail where CalWater has
completed work as there have been items left undone, such as tree stumps and an open
ditch. CALWATER REPRESENTATIVE WINJE indicated the work has not been completed

CALWATER REPRESENTATIVE WINJE stated that work continues but much of it is to be
concluded in July; however minor work, such as reseeding, will need to be revisited in
October and November and trails will be closed again briefly during that time.

MEMBER BRTS requested that the Equestrian Committee review the Trail Reconstruction
Plan and was further directed by CHAIR HUFF. CALWATER REPRESENTATIVE WINJE will
provide the plan for the next meeting.

Audience Member Bob Humphrey asked for more information about the brief trail closures
during the Fall; CALWATER REPRESENTATIVE WINJE indicated it is where the trail comes
to the Little League field. Two fences will be placed with 25 feet between the two
spots.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
June 24, 2019
 Member of audience expressed frustration that he is unable to move his horses back at the
end of June and is not certain if end of July is realistic with the continued CalWater work.
CHAIR HUFF requested that CalWater work individually with the member of the audience to
help find a beneficial solution.

Member of Audience Ken Anderson reported that he teaches at Dapplegray Arena and it is
very hard to water with the existing automatic valve. MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT
GOLDSMITH responded that this is on the list for maintenance to be completed this summer.

DISCUSSION ITEMS

5A. PORTUGUESE BEND NATIONAL HORSE SHOW (PBNHS) REQUESTED ARENA
IMPROVEMENTS

MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH provided an overview of the staff report; it
was reported that after the report was submitted for the Agenda there was additional
clarification needed from the event organizer as to what arenas they wanted enhanced
maintenance and that the Committee may want to table this item for future consideration until
more information is received.

Audience Member Pam Schachter requested clarification to confirm if proposed work was for
Arenas three and four, which needs additional maintenance. ASSISTANT TO THE CITY
MANAGER DAVIS indicated that staff is waiting for a written request providing that
clarification. MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH explained that rings will be
replenished in early July as part of regular maintenance.

MEMBER SHINN recommended that the Committee provide staff parameters to provide input
to event organizers as to what is likely to be approved.

MEMBER SILVANO asked if the City pays its employees to work the event and if the work
proposed needs to be completed in order to provide a safe event. MAINTENANCE
SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH affirmed that City staff is paid to set up, manage and tear
down the event and the request from event organizers is an enhancement to maintenance,
but the City does maintain the rings at EH by replacing and adding footing.

MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN

  THAT THE COMMITTEE RECOMMENDS APPROVAL OF MAINTENANCE
  ENHANCEMENTS AS PROPOSED TO ARENAS 3 & 4 BUT WITH ARENA 1 AND
  THAT CONSIDERATION SHOULD BE GIVEN TO WAIVING A PORTION OF FEES
  FOR A FUTURE EVENT IF MAINTENANCE IS APPROVED BUT IT IS IMPORTANT
  THAT COSTS ARE COVERED FOR CITY WORK.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN HUFF SO ORDERED.

5B. CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE COMPANY WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT
MONTHLY UPDATE

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
June 24, 2019
 Karina Winje from CalWater provided an overview of the project:

  •  Expected progress over the Spring months however ran into a scheduled delay due to
  a portion of the project needing a redesign
  •  Trail restoration has begun but not yet completed
  •  Ball field and work along Pony Lane will be completed in June
  •  Paving for ball field lot and access road will be in October/November
  •  There will be a minor closure during the Fall of that area

MEMBER SHINN asked if horses need to be moved again during the fall closure.
CALWATER REPRESENTATIVE WINJE responded no horses will need to be moved and
access will still be available via Rolling HIlls Road.

CHAIR HUFF requested that prior notification to the community be provided and that
CALWATER REPRESENTATIVE WINJE convey concerns addressed as necessary.

5C. EQUINE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS SUBCOMMITTEE REPORT

ASSISTANT TO THE CITY MANAGER DAVIS provided an update and reported that the
Horse Census has been finalized and will be launched in July/August culminating at the City
Celebration.

5D. MAYORS BREAKFAST RIDE DEBRIEFING

MEMBER SHINN reported that she and MEMBER CIAROLLA led the ride and the horses did
great; trails were well-maintained. CHAIR HUFF reported it was a fun event and well
attended.

5E. HORSE TRAILERING DEMONSTRATION UPDATE

MEMBER MARTIN reported that the event was not well attended and that another trainer held
another clinic conflicting with this one. CHAIR HUFF thanked him for the effort.

5F. BROWN ACT REVIEW

ASSISTANT TO THE CITY MANAGER DAVIS reported the training was held prior to the
Equestrian Committee meeting and was well attended with representatives from all of the
City’s committees and commissions.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH reported that issues reported have been
addressed.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIR HUFF RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

COMMITTEE REPORTS
  A. CITY CELEBRATION SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
June 24, 2019
 MEMBER SHINN reported that the group is working on the trail course. MEMBER CIAROLLA
reported that a western contractor has been hired. MEMBER SHINN also indicated that a face
painter has been confirmed and stick horse event is being coordinated. She also has shared
information with Channel 5 in hopes they can report about the event the day of. She
requested helpers for Gymkhana. MEMBER BRTS volunteered. MEMBER MARTIN reported
he is coordinating the poker ride and he is willing to help with Gymkhana. He additional
requested what the budget was for the DJ. ASSISTANT TO THE CITY MANAGER DAVIS
indicated she would look into that and report back. MEMBER SILVANO requested more
volunteers.

CHAIR HUFF thanked EC and members Silvano and Shinn for their recognition of retiring
Community Services Director, Andy Clark. ASSISTANT TO THE CITY MANAGER DAVIS
announced that a new staff person, Cynthia Morquecho, was hired as the Community
Services Supervisor and will start in June and Mike Goldsmith has been promoted to
Maintenance Superintendent.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIR HUFF RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
  A. PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILTIY PROJECT UPDATE – monthly

  B. CITY CELEBRATION UPDATE

  C. PORTUGUESE BEND HORSE SHOW PROPOSAL

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITEE MEETING

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIR HUFF ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:59 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Alexa Davis
Assistant to the City Manager

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
June 24, 2019
